wikiGoal:
# Benchmark documentation brief

Create a source-grounded wiki for engineers who must understand, operate, debug, and safely change this repository.

- Explain the architecture, ownership boundaries, core data/control flows, persistence, external integrations, configuration, and failure handling.
- Include a practical quickstart and focused change guides for representative maintenance tasks.
- Treat source code and tests as authoritative. Cite concrete source evidence for every non-obvious technical claim.
- State uncertainty when the repository does not establish a fact. Do not invent runtime behavior, guarantees, or deployment details.
- Prefer a coherent, non-overlapping taxonomy over exhaustive file-by-file narration.

pages.title: Classification: strategies, trees, and mixture of models
pages.purpose: Classification models and flow: Classification/ClassificationResponse, text vs vision classification, Process classification strategies (consensus/higher-order/threshold), tree classification via UUID, and layered mixture-of-models.
instructions: Document ClassificationResponseInternal confidence 1-10 contract and matching of returned name to the Classification object.
Document extractor group layers and consensus/higher-order/consensus-with-threshold semantics.
Document tree classification: level-by-level traversal, threshold validation, UUID-based node matching.

pages.title: Completion strategies: PAGINATE, CONCATENATE, and FORBIDDEN
pages.purpose: How long documents are handled when the output exceeds completion limits: the three CompletionStrategy values, PaginationHandler and ConcatenationHandler behavior, partial-output continuation, and LLM conflict resolution.
instructions: Document CONCATENATE: raw_completion JSON continuation with retry and cleanup, then model_validate.
Document FORBIDDEN: single request; incomplete/validation failures surface as ExtractThinkerError.
Document PAGINATE: per-page optional-model extraction in parallel, list-field merging by unique key, scalar conflict detection and LLM resolution via ConflictResolution.

pages.title: Document loader architecture and the page contract
pages.purpose: The DocumentLoader ABC and CachedDocumentLoader: capability checks, vision and pagination modes, PDF/image conversion helpers, cache semantics, the standard page-dict contract, and the config-dataclass pattern.
instructions: Cover the cachetools TTLCache caching with (source, vision_mode) keys.
Describe can_handle / can_handle_vision / can_handle_paginate semantics and how they gate Extractor and Process behavior.
Document the standard page list output contract (content/image/images/tables/forms/is_spreadsheet) and vision-mode attachment.

pages.title: Extraction pipeline: Extractor and the universal content format
pages.purpose: How Extractor drives loading, universal-format mapping, prompt building, LLM requests, and structured validation; vision mode, multi-source merging, completion-strategy dispatch, interceptors, and error handling.
instructions: Cover vision mode fallback to DocumentLoaderLLMImage and is_vision_error/classify_vision_error.
Detail _map_to_universal_format and the {'content','images','metadata'} shape and how list sources are merged.
Document completion-strategy dispatch and FORBIDDEN error mapping to ExtractThinkerError.

pages.title: LLM integration: backends, thinking mode, and dynamic parsing
pages.purpose: The LLM class: LiteLLM+instructor vs pydantic-ai backends, request vs raw_completion, thinking mode budgets, token limits, router usage, and dynamic prompt/JSON extraction.
instructions: Document DEFAULT backend (instructor.from_litellm MD_JSON) vs PYDANTIC_AI agent path.
Document is_dynamic parsing via extract_thinking_json and build_dynamic_prompt.
Document thinking mode: page_count -> thinking budget math, supports_reasoning gating, temperature=1.

pages.title: Markdown conversion
pages.purpose: MarkdownConverter: structured per-page conversion with certainty-scored JSON, free-form markdown conversion, basic non-LLM fallback, page filtering, and image placeholder handling.
instructions: Document PageContent/ContentItem certainty schema and placeholder instruction injection.
Document the three conversion modes and their LLM requirement differences.

pages.title: Architecture overview
pages.purpose: System-level map of ExtractThinker: component ownership boundaries, the universal page-based content contract, end-to-end data/control flow, extension seams, and the role of each major module.
instructions: Describe ownership boundaries (loaders own bytes->pages, LLM owns prompts/structured output, Extractor owns orchestration, Process owns split workflows).
Explain the pipeline as: source -> document loader -> universal page list -> Extractor merges/serializes -> LLM prompt -> instructor/pydantic validation.

pages.title: Process workflow and document splitting
pages.purpose: Process orchestration: load_file, split with EAGER/LAZY strategies, extraction per document group, splitter ABC, ImageSplitter/TextSplitter, and doc-group aggregation semantics.
instructions: Document extraction_contract vs contract selection in Process.extract and skip_loading flag usage.
Document the eager (whole-document classification into page groups) vs lazy (pairwise belongs_to_same_document then aggregate) flows and fallback behavior on LLM failure.
Note the >=2 page requirement and the pagination capability gate for lazy splitting.

pages.title: Change guide: adding a new document loader
pages.purpose: Focused maintenance guide for contributing a new DocumentLoader: subclassing, config dataclass, capability checks, page contract, caching, vision/pagination, exports, and tests.
instructions: Include the base test class contract and where to export the loader.
Step through the concrete pattern: config dataclass with __post_init__ validation, SUPPORTED_FORMATS, load() returning page dicts, cachedmethod, set_vision_mode.

pages.title: Change guide: tuning extraction behavior
pages.purpose: Focused maintenance guide for adjusting extraction: completion strategies for long outputs, thinking mode budgets, token limits, dynamic parsing, vision configuration, and per-loader cache TTL.
instructions: Document token_limit override vs DEFAULT_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS and thinking budget constants.
Show how to choose FORBIDDEN vs PAGINATE vs CONCATENATE and when each raises.

pages.title: Local loaders and OCR engines
pages.purpose: Local/in-process loaders: PyPdf, PDFPlumber, Tesseract, EasyOCR, Docling, MarkItDown, Spreadsheet, Txt, Doc2txt, BeautifulSoup, LLM Image, and Data loaders, including vision and pagination capability differences.
instructions: Note which loaders reject vision mode and how spreadsheet pages are flagged with is_spreadsheet.
Organize by capability (OCR, PDF text, office formats, web, data passthrough) rather than alphabetically.

pages.title: Managed document intelligence integrations
pages.purpose: Cloud/API loaders: Azure Document Intelligence, AWS Textract, Google Document AI, and Mistral OCR - configuration dataclasses, supported formats, feature flags, retries, and page output shape.
instructions: Describe each loader's credential requirements, validation in __post_init__, and retry semantics.
Document the enriched page fields (tables, forms, signatures, barcodes, formulas) each service produces.

pages.title: Batch processing with the OpenAI Batch API
pages.purpose: extract_batch flow: model support gating, JSONL input creation, file upload, batch creation, status polling/mapping, result parsing, and file cleanup.
instructions: Document BATCH_SUPPORTED_MODELS and can_handle_batch gating, the default extract_thinker_batch directory, and 24h completion window.
Document BatchJob lifecycle including get_status status mapping and get_result polling.

pages.title: Evaluation framework: metrics, hallucination detection, and CLI
pages.purpose: How to measure extraction quality: Evaluator and TeacherStudentEvaluator, dataset abstractions, field comparison types, metrics, hallucination detection strategies, cost tracking, report structure, and the CLI.
instructions: Document field metrics (precision/recall/F1/accuracy), comparison types EXACT/FUZZY/SEMANTIC/NUMERIC/CUSTOM, and hallucination = contradicted/total.
Document the extract_thinker-eval CLI entry point and setup.py console_script.

pages.title: Quickstart: ExtractThinker
pages.purpose: Hands-on entry point for engineers: installation, first extraction, classification, splitting, batch processing, markdown conversion, and pointers to where each subsystem lives.
instructions: Cover install from pyproject.toml and the public API re-exported in extract_thinker/__init__.py.
Trace each example back to its Extractor/Process methods so the quickstart doubles as a task-routing map.
